info.name: Cellphone Repair Shop API
info.description:
# Cellphone Repair Shop API

JSON API for a cellphone repair shop management system — repair intake and release, chain-of-custody proof, inventory across three item classes, point of sale, buy-back/refurb, and reporting. See `docs/design/01-domain-design.md` in the repo for the full domain design (ERDs, table catalogue, ticket state machine, error code catalogue).

This collection covers every endpoint implemented so far: health/readiness, auth, and the master-data contexts (branches, users, catalog, customers & devices). Later stages (repairs, chain of custody, inventory ledger, POS, buy-back, reporting) will extend this same collection as they ship — see the design doc §8 for the build order.

## Getting started

1. Make sure the API is running (`php artisan serve`) and `{{baseUrl}}` below matches it — defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1`.
2. Run **Auth → Issue Token** first. It authenticates against a seeded demo user (`ricardo.santos@fixmo.test` / `password` — the owner; see `database/seeders/UserSeeder.php` for the full roster across both roles and branches) and automatically stores the bearer token in the `token` collection variable. Every other request in this collection inherits it via collection-level Bearer auth.
3. Every **Create** request in this collection captures the new record's `ulid` into a collection variable on success (e.g. creating a branch sets `branch_ulid`), so the Show/Update/Delete requests below it work immediately without manual copy-pasting.

## Conventions

- **Envelope.** Success responses are `{ "data": ..., "meta"?: ..., "links"?: ... }`. Errors are always `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details" } }` — clients switch on `code`, never on `message` text.
- **IDs are ULIDs, not sequential ids.** Every path parameter *and every foreign-key field in a request body* (`branch_ulid`, `device_brand_ulid`, `product_category_ulid`, `compatible_device_model_ulids`, ...) is a ULID. The API never exposes the internal `BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT` id anywhere a client can see it.
- **Idempotency-Key.** Every write request here sends a fresh `{{$guid}}` as `Idempotency-Key`. Resending the exact same key with the exact same body returns the original cached response; the same key with a *different* body returns `409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. Try it: send a Create request twice with "Send" — Postman regenerates `{{$guid}}` each time by design, so to see the replay behavior, copy the header value from one request into the next send manually.
- **Pagination & filtering.** List endpoints return page pagination (`meta.current_page`, `meta.total`, etc.) and accept `filter[field]=value`, `sort=field` / `sort=-field` (descending), and `page=`. Each List request below has the allow-listed filter/sort query params present but disabled — enable the ones you want.
- **Permissions.** Endpoints are gated by the permissions seeded in `RoleAndPermissionSeeder` (e.g. `branches.manage`, `catalog.manage`, `reports.margin.view`). The seeded owner (`ricardo.santos@fixmo.test`) has every permission; try authenticating as a cashier or technician (see the seeder for emails, same `password`) to see `403 FORBIDDEN` and permission-gated fields (e.g. a product's `cost` field disappears entirely for a cashier) in action.

## Error code catalogue (implemented so far)

| HTTP | code | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `UNAUTHENTICATED` | Missing/invalid/expired bearer token |
| 403 | `FORBIDDEN` | Authenticated but lacks the permission |
| 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | ULID doesn't resolve, or resolves outside your branch scope |
| 405 | `METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED` | Verb not supported on the route |
| 409 | `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT` | Same `Idempotency-Key` replayed with a different body |
| 422 | `VALIDATION_FAILED` | Form Request failure; see `error.details[]` per field |
| 429 | `RATE_LIMITED` | Limiter exceeded |
| 500 | `INTERNAL_ERROR` | Unhandled throwable — still JSON, never HTML |
| 503 | `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` | `/ready` dependency (DB/Redis/queue) is down |

The full catalogue, including business codes for stages not yet built (`IMEI_MISMATCH`, `UNIT_ALREADY_SOLD`, `SHIFT_NOT_OPEN`, ...), is in `docs/design/01-domain-design.md` §5.

request.description: Issues a Sanctum bearer token. Every other request in this collection uses the `token` collection variable this sets automatically.
Controlled vocabularies the frontend would otherwise hardcode. Currently the repair-findings enums: root_cause, defects, resolution.

Branch-scoped key/value config resolved against the shop-wide defaults: each key is returned with its effective `value`, `type`, and a `source` of `branch` (this branch overrode it) or `global` (the shop default). Branch is always the caller's own. Requires `settings.manage`.

Partial bulk upsert against the caller's own branch. `settings` is a flat map of key => value; a key may also be the tagged form {"value": ..., "type": "string|int|decimal|bool|json"} to pin the type (otherwise it's inferred). A `null` value removes this branch's override, falling back to the shop default. Keys not in the payload are left untouched. Keys are open-ended (max 100 chars); receipt header/footer, TIN and VAT registration live as real columns on `branches`, not here. Requires `settings.manage`.

item.name: Branches
item.description: No destroy endpoint — closing a branch is `is_active = false` via Update, not a row removal (see design doc Flag 1). Requires `branches.manage` to create/update, `branches.view` to read (every seeded role has view).

item.name: Find My Branch (used by Users/Customers below)

request.description: Looks up the seeded owner's own branch (Quezon City, the demo user in Auth > Issue Token belongs here) and stores it as owner_branch_ulid. Deliberately NOT the branch created below — BranchScope hides records in a different branch than the authenticated user's own, even for an owner, so Create User/Create Customer need this branch, not a freshly created one, for the Show/Update requests underneath them to find anything.

item.name: Users
item.description: Requires `users.manage` to create/update/delete, `users.view` to read (owner + manager only in the seeded permission set).

request.description: role must be one of owner, manager, cashier, technician. Uses owner_branch_ulid (run Branches > Find My Branch first) rather than a freshly created branch — see that request's description for why.

item.name: Catalog
item.description: Requires `catalog.manage` to create/update/delete, `catalog.view` to read (every seeded role has view).

request.description: filter[device_brand_id] takes the brand's internal id, not its ulid, per spatie/laravel-query-builder's exact-match filter — a known asymmetry versus request-body fields, noted for whoever builds an SDK against this.
Run Device Brands > Create Device Brand first so device_brand_ulid is set.

`cost` only appears in the response for a user with `reports.margin.view` (the seeded owner/manager) — a cashier sees `selling_price` but not `cost`. category and brand are always eager-loaded; compatibleDeviceModels is opt-in via `include=`.
type is one of handset, accessory, part. Run Product Categories > Create and Device Brands > Create first so the ulid variables are set.

item.name: Customers
item.description: Requires `customers.manage` to create/update/delete, `customers.view` to read (every seeded role has view). mobile accepts common PH formats (09XXXXXXXXX, +639XXXXXXXXX, spaces/dashes) and is normalized to +63XXXXXXXXXX before storing.

body.raw:
{
  "branch_ulid": "{{owner_branch_ulid}}",
  "name": "Juan Dela Cruz",
  "mobile": "0917 123 4567",
  "email": "juan.delacruz@example.com",
  "address": "123 Mabini St., Quezon City",
  "notes": "Prefers SMS updates.",
  "is_blacklisted": false
}

request.description: Uses owner_branch_ulid (see Branches > Find My Branch) so the authenticated owner's BranchScope can actually see this record in the Show/Update requests below.

Shop-wide store-credit balance + the most recent ledger entries (newest first). Credit lands here from store_credit refunds, store_credit payments (as debits), and the manual adjustment below. Needs customers.view.

Manager/owner only (store_credit.manage). direction=credit grants, direction=debit corrects/claws back — 422 INSUFFICIENT_STORE_CREDIT if a debit exceeds the balance. Refund- and payment-driven movements go through the sales endpoints, not here.

item.name: Customer Devices
item.description: Nested under a customer. imei accepts raw digits or common separators, is normalized, and validated as 15 digits passing the Luhn checksum (App\Rules\ValidImei). Same customers.view/customers.manage permissions as Customers.

request.description: The default {{imei}} (490154203237518) is a well-known valid Luhn-checksum test IMEI. Run Customers > Create Customer and Catalog > Device Models > Create first.
404s if customer_device_ulid doesn't belong to customer_ulid — devices are checked against their parent customer, not just looked up globally.

Returns every customer_devices row for this IMEI across every customer — and every branch — that ever brought it in, not scoped to one customer or one branch. This is the differentiator described in docs/design/01-domain-design.md §2.3: a repeat repair is recognized even if the customer's first visit was at a different branch.

request.description: Uses owner_branch_ulid (see Branches > Find My Branch), not a freshly created branch — the authenticated owner's BranchScope needs to see the ticket in the Show/Update requests below. Run Branches > Find My Branch, Customers > Create Customer, and Customer Devices > Create Customer Device first.
Fails with 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION once the ticket has moved to released — edits are locked at that point.

Enforces the fixed state machine (docs/design/01-domain-design.md §4) — an illegal transition (e.g. straight to 'released') returns 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION with the allowed set in the error details.
Cursor-paginated append-only event ledger. Use the response's meta.next_cursor (per Laravel's cursorPaginate shape) as ?cursor=... to page further back.
The one findings record for this ticket (what was wrong, why, and what was done). 404 NOT_FOUND until PUT has been called at least once. tickets.view — cashiers can read.

body.raw:
{
    "summary": "Charging port pins corroded from liquid ingress.",
    "details": "Board otherwise clean. Ultrasonic cleaned, port flex replaced.",
    "root_cause": "liquid_ingress",
    "defects": [
        "charging_port",
        "sim_reader"
    ],
    "resolution": "part_replaced",
    "technician_notes": "Advise customer against non-original chargers.",
    "qc_passed": true
}

request.description: Upsert: 201 on first call, 200 thereafter — one record per ticket, edited in place. Every call appends a finding_recorded timeline event (that is what preserves history). qc_checked_at / qc_checked_by are stamped server-side when qc_passed first goes from null to a real verdict. root_cause=other or resolution=unrepairable makes `details` required. A released ticket returns 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION. Enum values come from GET /meta/enums. tickets.update.

item.name: Add Stock So The Part Line Below Can Consume It

request.description: A part ticket line now consumes stock on add (RepairTicketService::addLine()), so the product created back in Catalog > Products > Create Product needs an on-hand balance in the owner's own branch before the next request can succeed.
Run Catalog > Products > Create Product first. unit_cost is only visible in responses to roles with reports.margin.view.
Rule Zero: the response is JSON containing a ULID and a short-TTL signed url, never the binary itself. Select a JPEG/PNG file for the "photo" field before sending.
Sending a quote while the ticket is still "diagnosed" auto-advances it to "awaiting_approval".

An 'approved' decision locks approved_amount onto the ticket, recalculates its balance, and auto-advances it to 'in_repair'; 'declined' auto-advances it to 'returned_as_is' instead — both only when that transition is still legal from the ticket's current status.

Pays down the ticket's balance directly — a repair ticket is never wrapped in a Sale to collect payment (see TicketPaymentController's docblock). 500 is a safely partial amount regardless of how much of the quote flow above ran; check the response's data.ticket.balance for what's actually left, and call this again with that amount to fully settle it (required before Transition Ticket Status can move a ticket to 'released').

Records the scan whether or not it matches — matches_expected in the response reflects the comparison against the ticket's own customer_device.imei_normalized. A mismatch here doesn't fail the request; it's the release-time guard (see Transition Ticket Status → released) that actually blocks on it.

Owner/manager only (tickets.imei_override) — a self-contained, logged escape hatch for a mismatched or unreadable IMEI at release. Lets the ready_for_pickup → released transition proceed despite a mismatch.

A documentation-only chain-of-custody record of what physically came out and went in — not the billing line for it (see Repair Tickets > Add Ticket Line for that). installed_product_ulid should be a 'part'-type product.

The one unauthenticated endpoint in the API — proof a device genuinely passed through this shop's chain of custody. verification_token comes from Repair Tickets > Show Repair Ticket's data.verification_token (staff-only field, exposed so it can be embedded in a printed QR code). Deliberately redacted: no customer name, no claim_code, no pricing. Rate-limited to 10/min/IP regardless of auth.
product_ulid must reference a handset-type product (Catalog > Products > Create Product, with type=handset). Registering a unit also posts a +1 receipt movement — see Inventory > Get Stock Movements.
A status change is validated as a compare-and-swap and audited as a stock movement when it's 'written_off'. 'sold' is rejected here on purpose — that belongs to the (not yet built) sales flow.
Posts a -1 stock movement (movement_type=write_off) so stock_levels stays in sync with the true in-stock count.
The write path exercised for now while purchase orders/goods receipts are still pending (see routes/api.php). A line referencing a serialized_unit_ulid must adjust by exactly ±1.
A derived, never-authoritative cache — see stock_movements for the source of truth.
Cursor-paginated append-only ledger — the source of truth stock_levels is derived from. Use meta.next_cursor as ?cursor=... to page further back.
Starts in draft. Run Suppliers > Create Supplier and Catalog > Products > Create Product first.
Only draft→submitted, draft/submitted→cancelled are legal here — partially_received/received are system-derived by receiving, not settable via PATCH.

Posts a goods receipt for however much of each line arrived (can be partial — the PO's status becomes partially_received or received accordingly). Lines are keyed by product_ulid, not an internal line id (purchase_order_lines has no ulid).
Receiving without a purchase order backing it — e.g. an unplanned drop-off restock.
Opens a shift for the authenticated cashier (their own branch, inferred — not a request field). 422 VALIDATION_FAILED if they already have one open.
Cash in/out that never touches a sale — petty cash, change fund top-ups, bank deposits. Folds into expected_cash on close.

Requires an open shift (Shifts > Open Shift first) for the authenticated cashier. Computes VAT (see SaleCalculator) and consumes stock for track_inventory products — Catalog > Products > Create Product defaults to non-serialized with track_inventory=true, so register stock first (Inventory > ... or a Stock Adjustment) or expect 422 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK.

Call more than once to split a payment across methods (e.g. part cash, part gcash) — 409 PAYMENT_SUM_MISMATCH once the sum would exceed the total. tendered/change_given only apply to cash. method=store_credit draws down the sale customer's store-credit balance (422 INSUFFICIENT_STORE_CREDIT if short; the sale must have a customer). method=trade_in — see Trade-In Payment below.

Applies a customer's traded-in phone as tender. Run the Buy-back / refurb folder's Create Acquisition → IMEI Check → Complete Acquisition first (that sets acquisition_ulid and creates the serialized unit). offered_price caps amount; the acquisition can back only one sale — 409 TRADE_IN_NOT_AVAILABLE if it's not completed, is at another branch, or was already used. trade_in never touches expected_cash.

line_index refers to the line's position in Show Sale's data.lines array (sale_lines has no ulid of its own). restock puts it back on the shelf (or flips a serialized unit back to in_stock); no_restock/write_off both leave stock exactly as the original sale left it. refund_method: cash writes a drawer-out cash movement against your open shift (so Close Shift's expected_cash drops by the refund — needs an open shift); store_credit issues the total into the customer's store-credit ledger (the sale must have a customer); gcash/maya/card/bank_transfer are reversed out-of-band.

Reverses stock consumption (a serialized unit goes back to in_stock). Only a still-completed sale can be voided — running this right after Refund Sale above (on the same sale) correctly 409s, since that sale is now refunded, not completed; try it against a fresh Create Sale run instead to see it succeed.

Run this last — closing leaves the shift unusable for new sales/cash movements (409 SHIFT_NOT_OPEN afterward). expected_cash only counts cash payments and cash movements; run Sales > Add Sale Payment (cash) first to see a non-zero reconciliation.
A stateless preview — no sale is created. Try type=percent&value=10 for a plain promo discount instead. senior_citizen/pwd default their value to the legally-fixed 20% when omitted.

item.name: Sales Warranty
item.description: The shop (or manufacturer) warranty a serialized unit carries out the door when it's sold — wholly separate from the repair-ticket warranties under Repair Tickets. Run Shifts > Open Shift, then Serialized Units > Register Serialized Unit (leave it in_stock), then the requests here in order. A claim filed here stays under CP units and never opens a job order.

request.description: Needs an open shift and an in_stock serialized unit. A sale_warranties row is issued automatically for the serialized-unit line — term from the product's warranty_days unless warranty_days / warranty_coverage / warranty_terms override it here (omit them to use the catalog default; 0 issues nothing). The clock starts on the sale date. See List Sale's Warranties next for the issued ulid.
Every warranty the sale issued. Captures sale_warranty_ulid from data[0].
Every sale warranty ever issued for this unit — useful after a unit is returned, re-received and re-sold.

Files the claim against the sale warranty — it stays a sales-side record and never creates a repair ticket. within_coverage is stamped from the warranty's expiry at filing time (a lapsed warranty still records, just flagged false). Set handling to repair_board and add "repair_ticket_ulid": "{{ticket_ulid}}" to pin an existing job order for the bench work.

Ships the unit back to its vendor. Writes the stock ledger (a return_in +1 first if the unit was already sold, so the round trip nets to zero on-hand, then a return_out -1) and moves the unit to returned_to_supplier. The unit must currently be in_stock, sold or for_repair — 409 INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION otherwise. sale_warranty_claim_ulid is optional (a DOA unit that never sold has no claim).

outcome = replaced mints a fresh serialized unit (a normal receipt) and links it as replacement_serialized_unit; credited instead takes \"credit_amount\": 8500 and no replacement; rejected / closed take neither. Any still-open linked claim is carried to resolved / returned_to_supplier. Only a return still in \"sent\" can be closed.

item.name: Resolve Warranty Claim (alt to supplier return)

request.description: Closes the claim in place — use when the defect was handled without shipping the unit back (resolution one of repaired_in_house, replaced, refunded, rejected). If Close Supplier Return above already resolved this claim, this correctly 409s (claim already closed); run it against a claim you handled directly instead.

body.raw:
{
    "branch_ulid": "{{owner_branch_ulid}}",
    "seller_name": "Juan Dela Cruz",
    "seller_id_type": "Driver's License",
    "seller_id_number": "N01-23-456789",
    "declared_source": "Personal use, upgrading to a new phone.",
    "offered_price": 5000,
    "imei": "{{imei}}",
    "condition_assessment": "Good condition, minor scratches on the back.",
    "purchase_date": "2026-08-27"
}

request.description: Buy-back intake. imei_check_result starts not_checked — run IMEI Check Acquisition next.
A flagged result blocks Complete Acquisition (409 ACQUISITION_IMEI_FLAGGED) until re-checked clear.

Turns the acquisition into a real serialized unit (product_ulid should be a handset-type product) — that's when the shop finally identifies the exact model, after inspection. Idempotency: calling this twice on the same acquisition is a 409, not a second unit.
Requires the acquisition already completed (Complete Acquisition above). Moves the resulting serialized unit to for_repair for the duration of the job.
A part consumed by the job — posts a refurb_consumption stock movement and recomputes the job's parts_cost/landed_cost.
Moves the serialized unit back to in_stock and updates its acquisition_cost to the job's final landed_cost — the true cost basis for margin reporting going forward.
Splits (sale total − downpayment) evenly across term_months, one schedule row per month; the last row absorbs any rounding remainder. Run Sales > Create Sale (Product) first.

Also records a real Payment against the underlying sale (payable_type=sale) — one unified payments ledger, not a parallel one for installments. Adjust amount to match Show Installment Plan's data.schedules[0].amount_due.

item.name: Message Templates
item.description: Viber/SMS/email copy with `{{merge_field}}` placeholders, keyed by (channel, event_key). Config, not history — a retired template is `is_active = false`, there is no delete. All gated by `settings.manage`.

request.description: Every template. Filter with `filter[channel]`, `filter[event_key]`, `filter[is_active]`. Each row includes `merge_fields` parsed out of the body for the editor UI.

`channel` is one of viber|sms|email. `event_key` must be a known lifecycle hook (ticket.received, ticket.ready_for_pickup, ticket.released, ticket.unclaimed_30/60/90, quote.sent, warranty.expiring_soon, installment.due_reminder, installment.overdue). (channel, event_key) is unique — one template per hook per channel. Captures `message_template_ulid`.
One template by ulid.
Only `body` and `is_active` are editable — the (channel, event_key) identity is fixed once created.
Requires reports.margin.view (owner/manager only) — 403 for a cashier.
Requires reports.margin.view too, same as the margin report.

item.name: Cleanup (run last)
item.description: Every destructive request from the folders above, in reverse dependency order, plus revoking the token this run's Auth → Issue Token created. Deliberately kept out of the main top-to-bottom flow — running these mid-collection would delete/soft-delete records (Customers, Users, and every Catalog model are soft-deletable) that later folders still depend on via the ulid variables captured above; a soft-deleted record 404s on every subsequent lookup because of BranchScope/the default Eloquent soft-delete scope. Run this folder by itself once you're done exploring, or just leave it — it's harmless to skip since re-running the collection from the top always creates fresh records.

request.description: The one hard delete in this folder — CustomerDevice isn't soft-deletable.
A user can't delete themself — UserPolicy::delete blocks it (403). This is a different user than the one issuing the token, so it should succeed.

tokenId is the numeric id from Auth > List My Tokens (this is the one route that isn't ULID-keyed — Sanctum's own token model). Defaults to 1, which — in a single fresh run of this collection — is the same token Logout below revokes too; running both is redundant but harmless (the second is a no-op 401/404 against an already-gone token). Issue a second token first if you want to see this revoke a token you're not currently using.
Run this absolutely last — every request above needs the token this invalidates.
